title: MINLP formulations for continuous piecewise linear function fitting
contribution: Shows by two counterexamples that the coauthored 2014 MINLP for free-breakpoint linear-spline regression can fit a non-function, and proves three corrected formulations correct with equal optimal values, ordering constraints being fastest in Couenne.
problem_entry: Error in the team's own earlier model [5]: MINLP (1) is incomplete for general data; hidden because [5] only fitted concave/convex data and all tested datasets happened to give functions (pp. 2-4).
key_idea: Tiny synthetic counterexample (5 points, m=3) plus a real Titanium instance, then three repairs: assignment constraints (2), explicit breakpoint ordering (3), chained phi inequalities (4) (pp. 4-5).
assumptions: Sufficiently large finite big-M constants with data-dependent bounds; m <= n for equal optimal values; p = 2 in experiments (pp. 3, 7-8).
proof_devices: two-way correspondence proof between feasible points and continuous PL functions with explicit construction (6a)-(8) (Theorem 1, pp. 6-7)
feasible-region chain X_R ⊃ X_3, X_4 ⊃ X_S plus equal optimal values by moving an unassigned segment's breakpoint to the nearest data point (Theorem 2, p. 8)
experiments: JuMP + Couenne 0.5.6, 2-h limit, Titanium/Concrete/NHTemp, m=2-4, nodes and CPU time for all variants incl. the unrepaired model, LIMIT entries kept; ordering (3) usually fastest (pp. 9-10).
positioning: Corrects Goldberg-Kim-Leyffer-Veselka 2014 [5]; borrows constraint (4) from Rebennack-Krasko's convex MILP [9] and ordering from [8] (pp. 3, 5).
writing: Short correction note: abstract states the error plainly, two figures show the non-function fits, conclusion opens with 'We have pointed out an error' (pp. 1, 4-5, 10).
limits_future: Three small datasets, one solver, m <= 4; suggests ordering-based constraints for larger models such as [9] (pp. 9-10).

method_links.note: smallest breaking example plus real-data instance against the team's own published model, then redesign
repair is in the formulation; formulation variant decides solvability
time-outs kept as LIMIT in the comparison table

transferable: When a model was validated only on a special case, check which constraints that case implied for free; they are candidates for what is missing in general (p. 3).
Pair a 5-point synthetic counterexample with one classic real dataset that also breaks (pp. 4-5).
For several repairs, prove a feasible-region chain and an optimal-value equality, then benchmark all variants including the unrepaired relaxation (pp. 8-9).
coauthors: Noam Goldberg (first), Steffen Rebennack (corresponding), Youngdae Kim, Vitaliy Krasko

quotes.text: We have pointed out an error in the nonconvex MINLP for fitting piecewise linear functions proposed in [5].
In many real datasets including all of those experimented with in [5] and [9], the relaxed formulation (1) coincidentally computes a correct solution

title: A solution framework for linear PDE-constrained mixed-integer problems
contribution: For linear MIPDECOs, replaces discretized PDE constraints by FEM-precomputed superposition of control-basis states and imposes the dense state bounds as lazy constraints, solving 160x160 grids where the finite-difference MILP fails beyond 20x20.
problem_entry: Empirical bottleneck: discretize-then-optimize MILPs from finite differences are too large for CPLEX at useful accuracy; two-way coupling of PDE state and network decisions (pp. 1-3).
key_idea: Superposition over a control basis (|N|+1 PDE solves via time shifting) removes mesh-scaling state variables; lazy-constraint callback adds one most-violated grid bound per time step at incumbents (pp. 23-26).
assumptions: Linear well-posed PDE on a square domain, binary and L2 controls, linear bounded side constraints; time invariance used but not essential; chattering absence observed, not proved (pp. 4-6, 15-16).
proof_devices: no convergence theorems; reformulation correctness via superposition principle and time-shift identity (pp. 23-24)
lazy-constraint validity: incumbent violating none of them is optimal for the full model (p. 25)
experiments: CPLEX 12.8 + oFEM, 20,000 s limit, wildfire and river-contamination models: FD direct model fails beyond 20x20/21x21, FEM basis model up to 160x160/90x90, callback speedup up to 200x, mesh-dependence tables (pp. 25-29).
positioning: Within MIPDECO; contrasts with PDE-on-network work that has only one-way coupling; argues optimize-then-discretize unlikely for MIPDECO (p. 3).
writing: Conclusions state plainly what the method cannot avoid (time-resolution scaling) and what is missing (convergence, regularization) (pp. 28-31).
limits_future: Poor scaling in time resolution, no convergence analysis or regularization, sparse mesh-dependence evidence; future goal-oriented adaptive FEM (pp. 27-32).

method_links.note: MILP solver used through lazy-constraint callbacks rather than as a black box
reformulation (eliminating mesh-scaling state variables) before algorithm change
MIPDECO as a named class combining discrete optimization and PDE numerics

transferable: For linear PDE constraints, precompute states for a control basis and substitute the affine superposition into the MILP; with time invariance one PDE solve per control suffices by shifting (pp. 23-24).
Treat dense, largely redundant discretized state bounds as lazy constraints, adding only the most-violated grid point per time step at each incumbent (p. 26).
Report a mesh-dependence table (differing binaries and state distance to the finest grid) next to run times (pp. 27-29).
coauthors: Fabian Gnegel (first), Armin Fügenschuh, Michael Hagel, Marcus Stiemer

quotes.text: This poor scaling with the resolution cannot be avoided by our methodology.

Our approach demonstrates that eliminating the PDE constraints and variables whose number scales with the discretization size seems to be a viable method for solving MIPDECO approximations with high accuracy.

title: A method for convex black-box integer global optimization
contribution: Gives the first non-enumerative method (SUCIL) that certifies a global minimizer of a convex function evaluable only at integer points, using secant cuts valid on unions of cones, and shows certification is hard beyond n = 5.
problem_entry: Gap: B&B, Benders and OA need relaxations or gradients; integer DFO methods reach only mesh-isolated points; no method besides enumeration for unrelaxable convex integer black boxes (arXiv pp. 1-3).
key_idea: Secants through n+1 poised points underestimate f on a union of cones (conditional cuts); OA-like loop of lower-bound update and evaluation; enumerative look-up table plus trust region after the MILP encoding blew up (arXiv pp. 5, 9-12, 17).
assumptions: f convex on finite bounded Omega in Z^n, no evaluation off Omega (Assumption 1); authors concede knowing convexity of a black box is rare (arXiv p. 1).
proof_devices: finite termination + contradiction via valid pointwise lower bound (Theorem 1, arXiv pp. 10-11)
extension to reduced point sets provided one cut per remaining point (Theorem 2, arXiv p. 16)
2-D counterexample f = x1^2 - x1x2 + x2^2 showing unconditional secant cuts are invalid (arXiv p. 19)
experiments: 24 instances on [-4,4]^n, n=3-5; four SUCIL variants incl. two idealized oracle versions; vs DFLINT(-M), NOMAD(-dm) 3.9.0, MATSuMoTo (20 reps, given the optimum); profiles on evaluations to termination and to first optimum; SUCIL best on >65% for certification, DFLINT-M finds optimum first on >85% (arXiv pp. 16-18).
positioning: Frames Algorithm 1 as an outer-approximation analogue; contrasts with integer pattern search, direct search, model-based and surrogate B&B methods (arXiv pp. 3-4, 9).
writing: Discussion says the section order retells how SUCIL was reached; comparison hedged with 'merely demonstrate' (arXiv p. 18).
limits_future: Combinatorial growth of secant combinations, most cuts useless, binary domains need full enumeration, pruning-cut search posed as open Problem 1, storage limits (arXiv pp. 19-21).

method_links.note: outer-approximation bound loop carried into derivative-free integer optimization
hedged comparison, favourable baseline settings, metric where SUCIL loses reported

new_pattern_candidates.evidence: SUCIL-ideal1/2 use true f values to give a best case for point selection
MILP model (CPF) and its blow-up data kept in the paper; discussion retells the path to SUCIL

transferable: When cuts are valid only on regions, keep the lower bound pointwise in a look-up table instead of big-M binaries (arXiv pp. 11-13, 17).
Plot evaluations-to-first-optimum and additional evaluations-to-certificate separately (arXiv p. 20).
State an unsolved hard subproblem as a formal open 'Problem' (arXiv p. 21).
coauthors: Jeffrey Larson (first), Prashant Palkar, Stefan M. Wild

quotes.text: Hence, our results merely demonstrate that SUCIL provably converges to a global optimum and uses fewer function evaluations
The order of results in this paper tells the story of how we arrived at the implementation of SUCIL.

title: A bilevel approach for identifying the worst contingencies for nonconvex alternating current power systems
contribution: A branch-and-bound for the AC power-grid attacker-defender maximin that keeps the nonconvex AC equations, using a max-min swap for upper bounds and SDP for lower bounds, with a graded finite-termination guarantee, and shows SOC-relaxed approaches miss vulnerabilities.
problem_entry: KKT/dual single-level reformulations need lower-level convexity and CQs, so the literature relaxes AC flow and gets false negatives; asks how much vulnerability is missed (preprint pp. 2-3).
key_idea: Upper bound per node from the minimax (defender-as-leader) problem, rewritten single-level while keeping AC equations; lower bound from SDP relaxation; branch on the largest dual multiplier of x_l <= 1 (preprint pp. 10-13).
assumptions: A1 consistent physical bounds, A2 W ⊇ W_AC; slacks make the lower level always feasible and its value concave in x; node subproblems solved only locally by Ipopt (preprint pp. 7-8, 12, 18).
proof_devices: concavity of the value function as infimum of affine functions (Prop. 2.1, preprint p. 8)
minimax inequality bound phi(x_N) <= Phi_N <= Psi_N (Prop. 3.1, preprint p. 11)
case analysis over fathoming reasons giving SDP-optimality, AC-optimality or a vetted candidate list (Theorem 3.3, preprint pp. 12-14)
experiments: Julia MaximinOPF.jl/PowerModels.jl, Ipopt+MA57 and Mosek, IEEE 30/57/118/300, K=1-16, single core, 24 h; enumeration shows SOC/SDP zero values for attacks with positive AC value; ACBnB always slower than MISOC [53] but finds different candidate attacks on cases 57 and 300 (preprint pp. 14-20).
positioning: Contrasts with relaxation-based single-level reformulations (KKT, Lagrangian dual, SOC [53]) and with heuristic/metaheuristic AC approaches (preprint pp. 2-3).
writing: States in advance that the baseline will win on speed and that the experiment's purpose is accuracy; disclaims solver advocacy (preprint pp. 16-17).
limits_future: Global optimality of node subproblems not verified; Pegase 1354/2869 too slow; branching rules primitive; many PSVA extensions listed (preprint pp. 21-22).

method_links.note: expected loss on speed stated up front, customary measures reported, solver choice disclaimed
slack-for-feasibility and exact-penalty reasoning carried into the lower level (weak)

new_pattern_candidates.pattern: graded guarantee with vetted candidate list
new_pattern_candidates.evidence: Theorem 3.3 states the weaker certificate delivered when inner global optimality cannot be certified

transferable: For a maximin with a nonconvex inner problem, swap max and min for a valid node upper bound, then dualize the inner linear max over the attack polytope to get a single-level problem (preprint pp. 10-11).
Branch on the largest dual multiplier of binary upper bounds when integrality-based rules do not apply (preprint p. 12).
Before the algorithm comparison, enumerate small instances under exact and relaxed lower levels to show which answers change (preprint pp. 14-16).

quotes.text: The solution approaches based on convex relaxations of the lower-level defender problem can be expected to yield “false negatives” in terms of of identifying power system vulnerabilities.
It must be emphasized that we do not expect—at this stage of development—for ACBnB to be competitive with MISOC with respect to computational performance

title: Compact representations of structured BFGS matrices
contribution: Derives compact representations of the two structured BFGS updates of Petra et al. and builds limited-memory line-search methods (L-S-BFGS-M/P) that scale to large problems and need fewer iterations than unstructured L-BFGS.
problem_entry: Structured BFGS updates combining known and approximated Hessian parts are dense and lack compact forms, so they do not scale (arXiv pp. 5-6).
key_idea: Compact factored forms (Theorems 1-2), limited memory with four initializations, Sherman-Morrison-Woodbury solves, Moré-Thuente line search with extra condition s_k^T u_k > 0 (arXiv pp. 6-15).
assumptions: f twice continuously differentiable; SPD of the M-update needs SPD B0 and s_k^T u_k > 0; P-update may be indefinite and is tested (arXiv pp. 4, 7, 13).
proof_devices: relabeling reduction to the Byrd-Nocedal-Schnabel compact BFGS form (Theorem 1, arXiv p. 7)
induction on k with 2x2 block middle matrix (Theorem 2, arXiv pp. 8-9)
experiments: MATLAB; extended performance profiles on structured quadratics, 61/62 CUTEst problems vs full-memory S-BFGS, LIBSVM logistic regression, Poisson control, IPOPT L-BFGS on a quartic, ptychography n = 5,000 (arXiv pp. 17-30).
positioning: Extends Petra-Chiang-Anitescu structured quasi-Newton [20] and Byrd-Nocedal-Schnabel compact representations [6] (arXiv pp. 4-6).
writing: Contribution paragraph names the hard step (unwinding (6)) and the device (induction) (arXiv p. 6).
limits_future: No convergence analysis in the parts read; initialization rankings depend on spectrum (arXiv pp. 30-31).

method_links.note: continued work in the home continuous-NLP toolkit (weak)
own full-memory methods and IPOPT L-BFGS as baselines; fairness rule not stated beyond equal memory and tolerances

transferable: To find a compact form for a modified quasi-Newton update, look for a shift that maps it onto the classical update and reuse the known representation (arXiv p. 7).
Extend a standard line search with the one extra curvature condition the update needs, citing an existence result for such a step (arXiv p. 13).
coauthors: Johannes J. Brust (first), Zichao (Wendy) Di, Cosmin G. Petra

quotes.text: Unwinding the update formula in (6) is challenging, however by using an induction technique we are able to derive the explicit expression of the compact representation.
The structured methods typically require fewer total iterations than do the unstructured approaches.
